conviction_note: Findings sum to -6.2 and I emit -5.0: the 1.2-point haircut is for genuine two-sidedness I could not resolve (the H2-25 comparative really is depressed by GBP5.7m of identified non-repeating losses, Schroders added to 11.09% in June, and the stock is on ~11x the house broker's FY26E EPS), plus the fact that a weak H1 top line is already public in the FY25 annual report and so is partly in the bar. print_vs_bar (-8.0) is larger in magnitude than expected_move (-5.0) for exactly that reason: the miss is half-expected, the reaction is not. Sized against this name's own distribution rather than my certainty -- median |move| 10.5% over five observed prints, 4 of 5 negative, with -18.25% at last year's interims -- so -5.0 is roughly half a typical session move, which is where a ~45% probability of a guidance trim lands. Coverage is 3 analysts of whom 2 are house brokers (Shore Capital is NOMAD and joint broker, Berenberg joint broker), so there is close to no independent estimate and a confirmed change of tone moves more, not less.

findings.finding: The FY25 annual report discloses that Group sales for the four months to 30 April 2026 were approximately GBP26.1m against GBP32.6m in the same four months of 2025 -- down 20% and already including Barry M from 9 February -- while the same document identifies GBP5.7m of non-repeating losses in the 2025 comparative (GBP2.4m of US tariff-driven Christmas order disruption plus GBP3.3m from a large Technic customer entering administration). Net of the easy comparative, the house broker's FY26 revenue of GBP108.0m still requires an H2 of roughly GBP63.5m against a normalised H2-25 of about GBP61.5m, on a base that ran -20% for a third of the year; the FY25 report also shows the core business excluding Brand Architekts at GBP93.3m against GBP102m in 2024. I size the pair net at -3.0 rather than treating the -20% alone as a large negative, because the comparative genuinely is soft.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: This is the line that has moved the stock every time. 2025-09-10 interims cut FY guidance to GBP107-112m revenue and the shares fell 18.25%; 2025-02-06 trading update -19.17%; 2026-04-29 FY25 results, which carried this very four-month figure, -8.27%. The one positive print in the observed five (2026-02-09, +10.50%) was an acquisition headline, not a guidance line.
findings.original_quote: The difficult trading conditions experienced in 2025 continued in Q1 2026 with unaudited Group sales for the four months to 30 April 2026 expected to be approximately GBP26.1 million (four months to 30 April 2025: GBP32.6 million). ... the results for the year were negatively impacted by certain specific, one-off events as reported in the Group's year end trading update. These included: tariff volatility in the US, which disrupted the placing of Christmas gift orders and impacted regular business causing the loss of approximately GBP2.4 million of sales, and a large customer of the Technic brand going into administration, causing the loss of GBP3.3 million of sales.
findings.why_not_priced: It is public but it is not what the market is anchored on, and the anchoring was done by the company. The 2026-06-16 AGM Statement gave only a two-month window -- 'sales from 1 April to 31 May 2026 ahead of the same period last year' -- and no year-to-date figure at all, six weeks after the company had volunteered a four-month YTD number. Every piece of wire copy since June reports 'Q2 improves, full-year expectations unchanged'. If the arithmetic were priced, the stock would not have rallied 23.6% off 177p on 20 July to 218.6p, and the house broker's FY26 revenue would not still sit above FY25 actuals; with 3 analysts of whom 2 are paid by the company, nobody independent is publishing the H2 bridge.
findings.independence: The AGM Statement RNS of 2026-06-16 independently confirms the selective window and the H2-weighting language (https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/warpaint-london--w7l/agm-statement/9619508). The two halves of this finding rest on ONE document (the FY25 annual report) and are therefore filed as one net finding rather than two, per the one-document rule; the FY25 results RNS of 2026-04-29 carries the same four-month figure (https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/warpaint-london--w7l/results-for-the-year-ended-31-december-2025/9542864).

findings.finding: The board halved its own forward EPS hurdle. Options granted on 17 June 2026 at 220p vest only if 'the compound annual growth rate in the Company's Adjusted Basic earnings per share must exceed 5 per cent. over the three financial years commencing 1 January 2026'; the previous grant, 5 December 2024, required the same metric to 'exceed 10 per cent. over the three financial years commencing 1 January 2025'. Off the FY25 adjusted EPS base of 16.7p, a 5% CAGR is 19.3p by FY2028 -- below the house broker's FY2026 forecast of 20.0p. The remuneration committee is calibrating three years of incentives to an outcome the published FY26 number already exceeds, and it did so the day after the AGM statement reiterated full-year expectations.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior instance of an option-hurdle reset on this name to score. The line it predicts -- the FY26/FY27 outlook paragraph -- is the one that produced -18.25% (2025-09-10) and -8.27% (2026-04-29). Scored on that line, not on the grant itself.
findings.original_quote: the compound annual growth rate in the Company's Adjusted Basic earnings per share must exceed 5 per cent. over the three financial years commencing 1 January 2026, subject to the discretion of the Board
findings.why_not_priced: A 'Grant of Options and Director/PDMR Shareholding' RNS is the single least-read headline category on AIM, and the comparison that makes it informative requires note 23 of a 108-page annual report, where the 10% hurdle sits. No wire story, no aggregator and no trade-press item I found mentions either hurdle. If it were priced, the 338p sell-side target on a 218p stock would not be standing and the June 2026 grant would not have been struck at 220p with a lower bar than the December 2024 grant struck at 490p. I size it -3.0 rather than larger because a 5% CAGR is a common minimum vesting gate and because the Dec-2024 grant is 55% underwater, so part of this reset is mechanical repricing after a de-rating rather than a forecast.
findings.independence: The FY25 annual report, note 23, is the source of the superseded 10% hurdle and is a different document from the RNS: https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/624aac5eec2229318e2db5e8/6a0f1d8d188670864b239a43_260522%20Warpaint%20Annual%20Report%202025%20WEB.pdf . Fully independent of finding 1's evidence base (grant terms vs sales figures), though both documents are company-issued.

findings.finding: The baseline's free control is misreading what is priced. run_up_20d_pct is +0.24% and run_up_5d_pct -0.67%, but the stock bottomed at 177p on 20 July and closed at 218.55p on 22 September -- +23.6% -- and roughly a fifth of the volume that did it was the issuer's own bid. Treasury shares went from nil to 1,116,967 between 27 July and 16 September; the 1,020,364 bought after 3 August are 19.4% of the 5.27m shares that traded in those sessions, on a name whose median turnover is USD 384k a day. The RNS itself warned purchases 'could exceed 25 per cent of the average daily trading volume'. So the stock goes into this print at the top of a corporately-supported rally, not flat.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The one observed print preceded by a rally rather than a fall -- 2025-09-10 interims, after the stock had recovered through the summer -- produced the largest negative in the set at -18.25%. The two prints that followed weakness (2025-04-29, -3.70%) were milder. Small n, and stated as such.
findings.original_quote: Issued share capital: 80,787,321 ordinary shares; Treasury shares held: 1,116,967; the total number of voting rights in the Company is therefore 79,670,354
findings.why_not_priced: It is not a fact about the company, it is a fact about the measurement: the 20-day window starts on 24 August, three weeks after the rally had already happened, so every ranker that reads run_up_20d_pct sees a neutral name. Reconstructing it needs the weekly Transaction in Own Shares RNSs, the treasury share count in each, and the daily tape -- three sources no aggregator joins. If the market had priced the corporate bid out, September volume would not have collapsed to 58k-150k shares a day against 300-800k in July.
findings.independence: The daily tape is a different source and shows the same thing: https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/W7L.L?range=6mo&interval=1d (177p on 2026-07-20, 218.55p on 2026-09-22). This finding shares the buyback programme with the outside_window row below; the in-window content here is the price level going in, the out-of-window content there is the bid disappearing.

findings.finding: Barry M was bought on 9 February 2026 for GBP1.4m cash, including 'its IP, stock and order book, but excluding the manufacturing capabilities and any liabilities' -- a brand with GBP15-17.4m of annual turnover and one-metre-plus stands in 1,300 UK stores. No fair value allocation has ever been published: the FY25 annual report carries it only as a bare post-balance-sheet note. If the identifiable net assets acquired (inventory plus the order book plus brand IP) fair-value above GBP1.4m, IFRS 3 forces a gain on bargain purchase straight through the H1 income statement, which would flatter statutory PBT against a weak underlying half.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Barry M headline itself is the only positive print in the observed five: 2026-02-09 'Acquisition of Barry M brand & FY25 Trading Update' +10.50%, on a day that also carried a weak trading statement. So this market has paid for Barry M news before. No prior exceptional-credit instance to score.
findings.original_quote: On 9 February 2026, the Group acquired the Barry M brand, including its IP, stock and order book, but excluding the manufacturing capabilities and any liabilities, out of administration, for a cash consideration of GBP1.4 million, from existing cash resources.
findings.why_not_priced: Because the number does not exist anywhere yet -- the H1 accounts are the first time IFRS 3 fair values for Barry M will be published, and the FY25 annual report deliberately says nothing beyond the consideration. It is sized at a fraction of the same money in operating profit because it is a one_off with no stated path to the guide or the multiple; the company reports on adjusted EBITDA, which would exclude it, so the upside is confined to a statutory headline read by the RNS-reading retail half of the register.
findings.independence: Barry M's scale is corroborated outside the company: GBP17.4m turnover for the year to February 2024 and 1,300 stores (Superdrug 650, Boots 420, Sainsbury's 120, Tesco 50) per https://www.cosmeticsdesign-europe.com/Article/2026/02/12/warpaint-buys-barry-m-to-boost-uk-retail-reach-amid-tough-market/ . The exclusion of the London factory is the offsetting risk and is on the record in the same trade piece.

findings.finding: The TR-1 record shows the largest non-insider holder adding into the print and a smaller one trimming: Schroders plc went 10.040844% -> 11.086664% on 16 June 2026, the day of the AGM statement; Rathbones Investment Management went 5.575700% -> 4.996700% on 6 July 2026. Against a concert party (Bazini, Macleod, Rodol and relatives) of about 39.73%, that leaves a genuinely thin free float -- roughly 44% once Schroders and Rathbones are removed -- which is the mechanical reason this name prints double-digit reactions on USD 384k of daily turnover.

outside_window.finding: The GBP2.5m buyback is 89-98% spent and its bid disappears within about two weeks. Treasury reached 1,116,967 shares by 16 September; the 3 August tranche went at a 187.59p VWAP and everything after it traded in a 200-223p band, which bounds cumulative consideration at GBP2.22m-GBP2.46m of the GBP2.5m maximum. At the recent pace (86,371 shares in the week to 11 September, 50,685 in three days to 16 September) the authority is exhausted in early October, removing a buyer that has been ~19% of daily volume. Real and sourceable, and worth nothing to a one-session window.

The entire FY26 second-half case rests on events that settle after this print: the Dirk Rossmann pilot across 2,200 German stores (launched May 2026, reorder decision H2), the 'significantly improved' Walmart Christmas order, the Ulta Beauty online Christmas gift range, and Barry M's first re-sourced production run after the London factory was excluded from the acquisition. Christmas sell-through is a December/January fact.
